artifacts.summary: Adjudication of the three Phase-4 repair candidates with empirical probes; recommends candidate (a) per-branch fuel restructuring with a 4A/4B/4C statement-level replacement spec

bibkey_verification_status: verified: Fitting1983 (references.bib:211), Dyckhoff1992 (:218), GargGenoveseNegri2012 (:239), Massacci2000 (:1041); no new citations introduced
key_findings: Candidate (a) per-branch fuel: GO. Sufficiency shrinks to intWork-based per-branch budgets (intFuelExt = 4*(2c+1)*(WBound+1)+1), consuming only the already-proved intWork_drop + intCount_notMem_mono; termination is unconditional WF on (sum 3^fuel_i, pending.length) since all branching sites emit exactly 2 children (Rules.lean:259,262,280).

Handoff correction: '<= ~4,700-digit numerals for all corpus rows' is REFUTED for row 20 (s=19, chainBound=9,961,472, fuel ~13.0M digits) but the numeral materializes in 599 ms (probe), so (a) remains feasible with a new 4C lake-test timing gate.

Candidate (b) WF-on-measure: NO-GO as the repair; the decreasing_by obligation requires the unproven DP-2 (hNW) invariant inside the engine DEFINITION (intExpMeasure_step_lt needs hb at Scheme.lean:2583; hb-maintenance needs hnw at :2323); decreasing_by sorry would sorryAx-taint the whole procedure. Elective post-DP-2 cleanup only.

Candidate (c) proof/eval split: NO-GO; equivalence blocked because remaining fuel leaks into bPers via applyPersistenceFixpoint (Expansion.lean:363), per-row equivalence not kernel-checkable (let recs), and the split reintroduces the sorry-free-but-wrong-verdict hazard the corpus exists to close.
No global-scalar fuel of any size can work: branch count is worst-case exponential in |intUniverseExt| = Theta(WBound), so the repair must change fuel architecture, not constants.
Blast radius of (a): four engine-induction proofs need wrapper ports (closed_unsat ~690 lines is the largest); mitigated by parallel-build-then-flip (4A engine, 4B lemma ports, 4C flip+corpus gate).

Phases 6-7 simplify under (a): R1's hFuel becomes a per-branch intWork bound with fuel-0 discharge by omega; Phase 7's genuine-fixpoint consumption unchanged; Phase 2/3 assets (intCreatedChain_le, WBound, intUniverseExt family) verified engine-independent and untouched.

memory_candidates.content: Fuel-based tableau/decision engines in Lean: a global scalar fuel must bound TOTAL steps (branch count is worst-case exponential in the universe size), so when the universe is blow-up-sized (e.g. Theta(WBound) from blocking pigeonhole bounds) no materializable global fuel exists. Per-branch fuel lists fix this: per-branch step count is linear in the universe (intWork-style counting measure), termination becomes unconditional WF on (sum of 3^fuel_i, pending.length) when branching is exactly binary, and no invariants enter the definition. WF-on-the-semantic-measure engines are worse: they force invariant preservation proofs into decreasing_by, putting research-grade obligations on the definition's critical path where a sorry taints everything.

Lean 4 #eval bignum performance facts (probed on cslib toolchain): Nat.pow uses fast exponentiation - 20^9961473 (a 43-Mbit / ~13M-digit result) materializes in ~0.6 s; but every subsequent Nat op on such a numeral (decrement, +1) costs ~8 ms (full-copy scale), so a fuel-counting loop doing N steps on a huge fuel numeral adds ~8N ms. Budget test suites accordingly and gate with a wall-time criterion; feasibility envelope for doubly-exponential-derived numerals dies around 0.5 GB (e.g. subformula count s~25 for (s+1)^(2^s*s) shapes).
